title: Rapid GPU-Based Pangenome Graph Layout
problem: Pangenome graph layout algorithms are memory-bound with irregular data access patterns, making visualization of large multi-genome graphs computationally prohibitive and requiring hours of execution time.
motivation: Visualizing pangenome graphs is essential for understanding genome diversity in computational genomics research.
method: The authors characterize a pangenome layout algorithm to identify data-level parallelism and implement three GPU optimizations: cache-friendly data layout to reduce memory pressure, coalesced random states to improve access patterns, and warp merging to enhance GPU thread utilization. The solution is evaluated on 24 human whole-chromosome pangenomes.
key_novelty: Coordinated application of three GPU-specific optimizations (cache-friendly layout, coalesced random states, warp merging) to overcome memory-bound irregular access patterns in graph layout algorithms.
contributions: Performance characterization revealing substantial data-level parallelism in pangenome layout algorithms
Three key GPU optimization techniques addressing memory-bound irregular access patterns
Quantitative metric for scalable evaluation of pangenome layout quality
57.3x speedup demonstration on human pangenomes, reducing execution time from hours to minutes

metrics.other: execution time reduction from hours to minutes, no layout quality loss

limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed in abstract.
